subject: ClarityHealth — production error cascade & fallback oscillation after model v5a rollout
messages:
From: Emma Ross <emma.ross@clarityhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClarityHealth production — sudden 5xx/429 cascade after v5a rollout

Vivek —

Heads up: we started seeing a sharp spike in 5xx and 429s across our CL-Prod cluster right around 08:50 PDT after the v5a model + new 4-bit quant profile and kernel flip were deployed. The errors manifested as: repeated 429s, followed by timeouts at the app layer, then many client retries which produced a throughput collapse on a subset of endpoints.

Impact: several critical search and summary flows returned errors for ~20 minutes; our telemetry shows request success-rate fell from 99.4% to ~81% during the worst window. We had to toggle client-side retry backoff to reduce blow-up.

What we’ve observed:
- Error codes: 429 spikes followed by 5xx (502/504) timeouts
- Seeded to a particular model variant: requests that route to model:v5a-quant4-alpha were 95% of the failed traffic
- Retries made the latency tail worse — we saw multiple concurrent downstream connection retries at the same P95 windows

We need immediate mitigation (traffic cut, fallback, or rollback) and we need to understand whether the quant profile or kernel change caused a serving regression. Customer-facing impact is real — our support teams are fielding calls. We also need a post-incident plan and an ETA for full recovery.

Attaching a screenshot of errors and a short trace.

Attachments: clarity-prod-5xx-sample.png

Can you confirm next actions and whether Redwood can cut traffic off v5a and route to the previous model while you investigate?

Thanks,
Emma Ross
Director, Platform Integrations
ClarityHealth

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma.ross@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClarityHealth production — sudden 5xx/429 cascade after v5a rollout

Emma —

Thanks for the clear report and the screenshot. Were treating this as SEV-level. Immediate plan Im initiating now: 

1) Temporarily pin ClarityHealth traffic to model:v4.9-stable (previous variant) — routing change in-flight (expect 2–5 minutes to propagate).
2) Disable the new 4-bit quant profile for the ClarityHealth tenancy (prevent kernel path that may be triggering regressions).
3) Engage a circuit-breaker on their per-route retry budget to limit client retries for 5xx/429 to reduce retry storms.
4) Collect and upload full serving traces and kernel logs to the incident Jira (INF-8723).

If you approve, I will go ahead and execute the routing pin + quant disable. We will also keep you updated every 20 minutes until stable.

Im copying Marissa and Laura to keep commercial and SRE loops tight.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre-oncall@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClarityHealth production — proposed hotfix and mitigations

Vivek / Marissa —

Standby status update from SRE. Ive read the traces — symptoms line up with a kernel selection path that increases memory pressure for small-batch streaming requests which then tied into our retry window behavior. Plan Im executing now (will update inline):

A) Traffic: pin the tenant to model:v4.9-stable (done by routing flag).
B) Quantization: disable v5a 4-bit quant profile for the tenant (deploying rollout protect).
C) Kernel: disable auto kernel flip for the affected shard group (hotfix in prod; rollback safe).
D) Retry/timeout tuning: temporarily lower client retry budget to 1 and shorten P95 timeout by 200ms for the affected routes to reduce amplification.
E) Dedicated routing: we are moving critical endpoints to a dedicated capacity pool for 30 minutes to isolate performance while we validate.

Ive created JIRA INF-8723 and attached a cut of the runbook (runbook_hotfix_v1.pdf). Actions will be executed in the order above; I estimate containment within 15 minutes of routing changes. Ill push a detailed timeline into the ticket.

—Laura
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma.ross@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, SRE Team <sre-oncall@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Status update — routing pin + mitigations applied

Emma — quick update: we performed the routing pin to model:v4.9-stable and disabled the v5a 4-bit quant profile for your tenancy at 09:58 PDT. We also disabled kernel auto-flip on the affected shard group and applied the retry budget change.

Current observations (09:58 → 10:18):
- 5xx rate for the impacted endpoints dropped from ~12% to ~1.1%
- 429 spikes have subsided and P99 tail latency improved by ~420ms
- Some minor oscillation observed as older clients continue to hit cached routes; that should settle within 30–45 minutes as caches expire.

Next steps: monitor for 2 hours, then perform a controlled canary of a patched v5a variant with more conservative quant settings and kernel guardrails. We will provide a full incident timeline and root cause analysis once the logs are fully aggregated.

I will keep you updated every 30 minutes until we reach steady state.

—Vivek
